Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — hosting deployment evidence needed

Hi Elena — attaching a compact evidence matrix and a responsibility summary to help the SIG reviewers. Quick summary below; full details in the spreadsheet (attached: sig-deployment-evidence-matrix.xlsx).

High-level responsibility split (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood manages compute, kernel/runtime, and infrastructure; data at rest is encrypted with customer-scoped keys in our KMS (for paid tiers we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration); network egress is controlled by our egress policies. Customers are responsible for tenant-level access controls and prompt/data classification.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools logically isolated for the customer. Redwood provides the same runtime but within a dedicated tenancy. Customers can opt into customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and stricter IAM boundaries. We provide audit logs and per-token telemetry; retention is configurable per contract.
- Private/VPC & On‑Prem: Customer-managed network and (optionally) control plane. For VPC deployments we run a customer-isolated control plane in their cloud account (Redwood-managed or self-hosted). For on-prem installs the customer controls all networking, keys, and physical isolation; Redwood provides the runtime package and operational runbooks.

Evidence pointers included in the spreadsheet:
- Encryption at rest: proof-of-architecture diagrams + KMS integration screenshots (Hosted/Dedicated) + guidance for on-prem keying.
- Audit logs: sample retention policy, schema of audit events, and a sanitized log sample.
- Network diagrams: per-mode flow diagrams and recommended firewall rules.

Attachments:
- sig-deployment-evidence-matrix.xlsx (matrix + links to artifacts)
- redwood-hosting-responsibility-matrix.pdf (one-page summary) [attached] 

If your security team needs us to sign a non-disclosure or share a sanitized log sample, we can arrange that (SEC ticket: SEC-1298).

Best,

Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.ai]

Jasmine — thanks, that matrix looks helpful. Two quick clarifications from our security team:  
1) For Hosted: do you offer a Customer-Managed Key (CMK) option for encryption-at-rest on the standard hosted tier, or is that only for Dedicated customers?
2) For Dedicated: can you confirm whether audit logs include per-request metadata (caller identity, model id, timestamp, token counts) and what the default retention window is?

Cc'ing our security mailbox so they can confirm the tape of evidence they'd like attached.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Hi Elena / team — looping in specifics so you can attach them into the SIG answers. Short answers below and I've attached a one-page PDF (redwood-hosting-responsibility-matrix.pdf) that you can include.

1) CMK availability:
- Hosted (standard): CMK is available on our paid hosted tiers when customers enroll in the KMS integration option. It's not the default for the free/trial tier. The spreadsheet points to the KMS integration guide and a screenshot from the console showing a CMK-bound dataset.
- Dedicated: CMK is supported and commonly used; we also support external HSM for certain enterprise contracts.
- Private/On-prem: Keying is customer-controlled; our on‑prem package includes guidance for integrating customer HSMs.

2) Audit logs and retention (Dedicated default):
- Logs contain per-request metadata: requestor identity, route/model id, timestamp, prompt token count, response token count, and routing decisions.
- Default retention (Dedicated): 90 days; retention can be extended to meet contractual needs (up to 3 years) as an add-on.
- Hosted default: 30 days for operational telemetry; export options available for longer retention.

Attachments included: redwood-hosting-responsibility-matrix.pdf (contains responsibility table and dataflow diagrams). Also shared link to SEC-1298 which has the sanitized log sample and audit schema.

On the SIG answers themselves, recommended phrasing for the question about 'who is responsible for key management' is included in the spreadsheet (column: suggested-sig-text).

Let me know if you need us to produce a signed evidence bundle (PDF + sanitized logs) for vendor risk.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
